statement: A salesperson earns a base pay of $\$2{,}100$ per month plus a commission of $6\%$ on the part of her monthly sales above $\$15{,}000$. There is no commission on the first $\$15{,}000$. What is the minimum amount of sales she needs in a month to earn at least $\$3{,}000$ that month?

choices.misconception: I took $6\%$ of all her sales, so I solved $2{,}100 + 0.06s \ge 3{,}000$ and got $\$15{,}000$.
I forgot about the base pay and made the commission alone reach $\$3{,}000$, so $0.06(s - 15{,}000) \ge 3{,}000$ gave $\$65{,}000$.

hints: How much of the $\$3{,}000$ has to come from commission?
The commission must make up $3{,}000 - 2{,}100$. Commission is $0.06$ times the sales above $\$15{,}000$.
Solve $2{,}100 + 0.06(s - 15{,}000) \ge 3{,}000$: the commission part must be at least $\$900$, so $s - 15{,}000 \ge 900 \div 0.06$.
